q1_issues.issue: `(Location sk_say_1 sk_statement_1)` treats "in a prepared statement" as a place, but it names the medium the claim was made in — the instruction set routes such a framing PP to the preposition-named oblique `(In ...)`, never to `Location`.

`(For sk_pref_1 sk_achieve_1)` uses a preposition-named oblique for a preposition that is not in the text; "Our preference IS TO achieve" is a copular clause, and the rule is that the head must be the preposition actually used.

The appositive typing `(Member marce_fuller ceo)` is emitted bare, but the appositive rule gives it the host clause's wrapper — the host "Marce Fuller said" is past, so `(Past (Member marce_fuller ceo))`.

`(Possession sk_pref_1 mirant)` for the quoted "our" is asserted at top level, though it is a predication inside the sealed quotation; the sealing rule projects only the definite referent's typing atom.

q2_gaps: a copular clause whose predicate is a to-infinitive ("Our strong preference is to achieve X") — neither the categorical section nor the control-verb pattern covers a specificational copula, and the parse has to invent a link to attach the infinitive

direct/verbatim quotation as a speech verb's complement — the propositional-attitudes section is written for a finite "that"-clause, and says nothing about whether a quotation's contents seal the same way or whether the quotation marks themselves are recorded
a sub-day qualifier that is not one of the listed day-parts ("early Friday") — the parse extends the day-part pattern with a bare `early` symbol on `Time`
notes: The `OutOf` multi-word preposition, the adjectival `prepared` (unfused, per the laminated-worktop rule), the `(Weekday friday)` term, and the non-factive seal under `say` all follow the instruction set.
